title: Msty Studio on a 24 GB Mac: It Found My Ollama Models at Once, What It Is For Stayed Unclear to Me
dek: Hands-on test on an M3 Mac with 24 GB. Existing Ollama models appeared without a second download. No image was generated.

seo.title: Msty Studio Hands-on Test: Ollama Models Found at Once
seo.description: Hands-on test of Msty Studio on a 24 GB Mac: Ollama models appeared at once, a file upload looped, no local image model worked in Media Studio.

faq: Does Msty Studio work with Ollama?

Yes, in this test. After Ollama was added as a provider, five Ollama models appeared in the model picker, and the notes record no second model download. The tester first believed the connection had failed.
Can Msty Studio generate images with a local Ollama model?

Not in this test. Media Studio opened, but the tester found no way to use his local image model (x/flux2-klein) there, and no image was generated. The contents of the 'Select image/video model' menu were not captured, and hosted providers were not tried.
Does Msty Studio say whether a model fits my Mac?

Model cards in the Model Hub carry a hardware hint, for example 'Should run fast on this Mac · ~3.2 GB memory needed, 16.8 GB available' on Qwen3-VL 4B. The estimate is the app's own; the model was not run.
How much does Msty Studio cost?
The vendor's price list, read on 16 October 2026, shows Free at $0, Aurum at $149 per user per year and Aurum Lifetime at $349 one-time. The plan the tester used is not recorded.

verdict.general: Partly tested. What the tester tried mostly worked: Msty picked up his existing Ollama models, a text chat and an image upload ran, and the Model Hub says whether a model fits the Mac. What did not come together: the website and first screens do not say what the app is for, a file upload looped between a knowledge base and the chat, and no image model could be used in Media Studio. The notes stop at the Model Matchmaker without a conclusion on Msty.
verdict.fit: Not recorded. The tester's own question, 'why should a home user use it', is not answered in the notes. The closing judgment in the Word file describes a different app and is not used here.

chapters.title: The website: what is it for?
items: The tester started on the Studio product page. Headline: 'One private AI workspace for real work.' Sub-line: 'Chat with models, organize knowledge, create media, and reuse prompts in one privacy-first workspace.' Button: 'Download Studio'.

He wanted to understand what Msty is about: it is 'one of the early ones, one of the professional ones', and for a home user he was not sure what the point is. 'The screen makes it clear that it's not clear what it's actually for.'
The tester saw several solutions and products and chose 'Download Studio' because it seemed to be the one that runs locally.
The vendor's product page names Studio, Go ('bounded AI agents'), Nexus ('AI control center') and Stack ('governed knowledge layer'). Checked on 16 October 2026; the tester did not open these.
The download file is 246 MB. The tester: 'so it's okay'.

His hope was an Ollama or LM Studio connection so that no further model download is needed. In his view every app should offer that choice next to built-in models, because 10 to 20 GB per app is 'just not the way forward'.

chapters.title: First launch: one local model or a provider
items: The first screen (Figure 1, top of this page) offers a card tagged 'LOCAL AI · RUNS ON YOUR MACHINE': Gemma 4 E2B, 3.6 GB, described as Google's compact multimodal model with vision. A strength slider runs from Light to Powerful and sits at 'Capable'. The button reads 'Download & Get Started'.

Below it, 'Or connect an AI provider' shows OpenAI, Claude, xAI, Gemini, OpenRouter and 'More'. A yellow notice reads 'Add at least one model before continuing with a connected provider.' and 'Continue with connected provider' is greyed out.
'Runs on your machine' is the app's own label. The tester did not download this model (he used models already in Ollama) and did not check network traffic.
The notice appears because no model had been added at that point. Which action enables 'Continue' was not tested.

chapters.title: Connecting Ollama
items: The 'New Model Provider' list groups Msty Remote and Ollama under 'Msty Compatible', MLX Remote under 'MLX Compatible' and LLaMA.cpp under 'OpenAI Compatible'. The list in the screenshot is scrolled, so entries above xAI are not visible.
Notes: 'It allowed me to connect to Ollama, select Ollama, but then it didn't select it.' He went back to the local-download screen to see what was going on.
The connection had worked. The tester did not realize it because, in his words, the app shows the model name and not the word Ollama. The picker then listed five models under an Ollama header.
Correction to the notes: the picker screenshot does show an 'Ollama' header over the list. The notes probably refer to an earlier screen that was not captured (assumption).
The tester's stated hope was met: his existing Ollama models were usable and the notes record no further model download.
The ':cloud' suffix on minimax-m2:cloud suggests a model that runs in the cloud and not on the Mac. Not verified. If so, the Ollama list mixes local and cloud models without a visible marker.

chapters.title: Chat tests
items: The tester asked for a QR code (prompt text not recorded; the reply refers to www.promptquorum.com). The reply said it is a text-based AI that cannot generate images, and gave five steps for using a free online QR generator.
52.81 tok/s is shown under the reply. The model name is partly cut off ('gemma4:latest' visible at the top; the match is likely, not certain).
A text model was asked for a picture. The reply was correct for a text model. The tester framed it as 'the difference to a functional model'.
The tester then selected an image model from earlier work (x/flux2-klein in Ollama) as the chat model. Per the notes, it 'does not support chat'. The message itself was not captured.
The tester doubted that two or three models can be loaded at once ('I don't think so'). Not tested. The vendor page lists 'Split Chats: run models side by side'.
Back on gemma4:latest he uploaded a picture and the model could read it (notes only; the picture and the answer were not recorded).

chapters.title: Uploading a Search Console file
items: The tester uploaded a Google Search Console export. According to the notes the app 'just ran' an analysis without being asked. The first point of the advice, as quoted in the notes: 'Investigate High-CTR Regions: A rapid audit of Gambia, Saint Barthélemy, Bangladesh, and Gabon is essential.' The numbers were not checked against the file. Model and file size not recorded.

The loop, as described: uploading puts the file into 'some background tool, knowledge base'. Back in the chat, the app analyses automatically and gives no chance to say what to analyse. Typing 'I want this analyzed' in the chat makes the app ask for the data.
The Knowledge Stacks screenshot follows these notes. That the file went through Knowledge Stacks is the tester's reading ('knowledge base'), not confirmed.

The Knowledge Stacks screen offers: new stack, discover curated stacks, import .mstyks files, and 'Switch back to Classic Knowledge Stack'. Sources shown: Notes, YouTube Links, Web Links, Conversation Projects, Conversations; a row partly cut off at the top appears to read 'Folders & Obsidian Vaults'.
'Okay, this goes in circles.' Then: 'So this looks like an interesting tool, but let's see.'

chapters.title: Media Studio
items: The sidebar has a 'Media Studio' entry. The screen reads 'Create images and videos that follow your imagination wherever it leads.' It has an optional context drop zone, a prompt box ('Describe your creation...'), a counter set to 1 and a menu reading 'Select image/video model'.
'Great, can do pictures too.' But when connecting to his local LLM setup, the app said his Ollama has no picture model, and he thought Flux was the right one.
No image was generated in Msty. The notes record no image-model selector that worked for him.

Media Studio does not list the Ollama image model x/flux2-klein. The contents of the model menu were not captured. The vendor changelog dates Media Studio to release 2.7.0 (29 April 2026) and mentions xAI and OpenRouter image and video models, which suggests hosted providers. Not verified.

chapters.title: Model Hub and Model Matchmaker
items: The Model Hub sidebar lists Model Providers, Local Models, Model Squad, Model Matchmaker, Model Cost Calculator, VRAM Calculator and Context Explorer. Local Models has tabs Featured, Installed, Search and Import. Only the Matchmaker was opened, per the notes.
Model cards show size and quantization. A tooltip on Qwen3-VL 4B (2.4 GB, 4-bit) reads 'Should run fast on this Mac · ~3.2 GB memory needed, 16.8 GB available'.
That fit estimate is the app's own. The model was not run.
'Model Matchmaker. Great idea. I like it.' But he found no selectors for picture generation.

The next screenshot shows the Matchmaker's ranked list: #1 claude-opus-4-6-thinking-auto-high-effort and #2 claude-opus-4-5-20251101-thinking-64k-high-effort, both 'Anthropic /remote', score 100. A notice 'Setting up MLX: Preparing engine setup...' is visible; why it appeared was not recorded.
'In October 2026 and I see this, I'm not impressed. That is an AI process to update this. I have tools on my website to update the website. Why is it so difficult?'
'This' is read here as the ranking in the screenshot being out of date. The notes do not say which screen he meant.

Anthropic's models page (checked 16 October 2026) lists Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) as the newest Opus and does not list the two 4.x models as current. The ranking's data date is not shown in the screenshot, so whether it is stale is not confirmed.

Visible Featured models are Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3, Llama 3.2 3B and 1B, Meta Llama 3.1 8B. Mistral 7B at 6.9 GB is larger than Llama 3.1 8B at 4.5 GB, both labelled 4-bit; the difference is not explained on the cards.

Not recorded for Msty: app and macOS version, end time, plan used, a verdict, an uninstall check.

findings: The Studio page and first screens do not tell a home user what the app is for.
First screen offers one local model (Gemma 4 E2B, 3.6 GB) or a hosted provider; Ollama is not shown there and appears in the provider list instead.
Existing Ollama models appear in the picker; the tester's hope of avoiding a second model download was met.
After connecting, the tester could not tell that Ollama was connected (the notes mention no confirmation).
Image-only (x/flux2-klein) and ':cloud' models are listed together with chat models; the image model did not work for chat.
A text model answered an image request in a sensible way and pointed to an online generator.
Image upload to gemma4:latest worked, per the notes.
File upload looped: automatic analysis without a question; a chat request asked for the upload again.
Knowledge Stacks offers several source types and an import format (.mstyks); only the start screen was seen.
No local image model could be selected in Media Studio; no picture was generated.
Model cards show a hardware-fit hint with memory needed and memory available.
Model Hub bundles seven tools (providers, local models, squad, matchmaker, cost, VRAM, context); only the Matchmaker was opened.
Matchmaker ranking led by two Claude Opus 4.x models while Anthropic lists Opus 5.5 as newest; staleness not confirmed (no data date shown).
'Setting up MLX' notice appeared with no recorded trigger.
Mistral 7B (6.9 GB) is listed larger than Llama 3.1 8B (4.5 GB), both '4-bit', without explanation.
The tester rated the Model Matchmaker idea highly and the tool 'interesting'.
severity_note: Severity is the impact on a first-time user. Proposed, not measured.

fits: People who already run Ollama and want one desktop front end for local and hosted models (Ollama reuse worked in this test).
Teams that need SSO, audit logs and shared controls (listed on the vendor's Studio page; not tested).
not_fits: A home user who wants to understand from the first screens what the app is for.
Users who expect to generate images in Media Studio from a local Ollama image model (did not work in this test).
audience.retest: Retest the untested parts (Split Chats, prompts, Media Studio with a hosted image model, the file workflow, uninstall) and record version and macOS first. The vendor changelog shows 3.0.0 still in beta on 7 October 2026, so the interface may change at release (assumption).

Price list: Free $0; Aurum $149 per user per year; Aurum Lifetime $349 one-time; Enterprise and Teams on request, minimum 5 seats. The pricing page does not state a software license.
The PromptQuorum directory lists Msty as closed source, freemium, for macOS, Windows and Linux, last upstream update 7 October 2026. The listing has not been verified (freshness: unverified).

Changelog: Media Studio introduced in release 2.7.0 (29 April 2026); MLX support for Apple Silicon first appears in 2.0.0-alpha.10 (7 August 2025), marked experimental; Knowledge Stacks 2.0 in 2.0.0-alpha.9 (31 July 2025). Latest listed on 7 October 2026: 3.0.0 Beta 15.
